isolation: Signed in once as test-cook-1 (Maria, role Cook). Each CRUD scenario creates the specific recipe it asserts about through the app's own UI and asserts on that recipe by title, so the assertion holds regardless of what else is in the account. Recipes created in one scenario (Grandma's Chili, Pancakes, Garden Salad, the imported '** Lemon Bars') persist into later scenarios whose Given steps name them, matching the feature file's own narrative ordering. Where the product has no per-scenario container (the empty-meal-plan and discard-draft scenarios), the assertion is a before/after delta on the recipe-row or shopping-list-item count rather than an absolute total, since this run was the only writer against the account for its duration.

scenarios.rule: A Cook can have a recipe extracted automatically from pasted text or a recipe URL
scenarios.scenario: Extracting a recipe from pasted text

steps.text: Maria has pasted recipe text for "Lemon Bars" including its ingredients and steps
Maria asks the agent to extract the recipe
the agent returns a draft recipe titled "Lemon Bars" with its ingredients and steps filled in
steps.observed: "** Lemon Bars" — a literal "** " markdown-bold artifact prefixes the title instead of it reading exactly "Lemon Bars"; ingredients and steps fields were correctly filled in (1 cup flour / 1/2 cup butter / 2 eggs / 1 cup sugar / 1/3 cup lemon juice; the two bake steps)

scenarios.rule: A Cook can have a recipe extracted automatically from pasted text or a recipe URL
scenarios.scenario: An unreachable recipe URL is refused before extraction

steps.text: Maria submits the unreachable URL "https://example.invalid/no-such-recipe"
Maria asks the agent to extract the recipe
steps.observed: POST /api/recipe-import-agent/chat -> 422 {"error":"Violation of url validity detected.","guardrail":"url-guardrail"}; stayed on /import

steps.text: no draft recipe is produced and Maria is told the link could not be reached
steps.observed: no draft shown (correct), but the banner reads "The import agent could not be reached. Try again." — this tells Maria the AGENT service is unreachable, not that her LINK could not be reached, even though the backend's own 422 response shows it did reach the agent and reject the URL via its own url-guardrail. The webapp collapses this 422 into the same generic message it would show for a real connectivity failure.

scenarios.rule: A Cook reviews and edits an agent-extracted draft before it is saved

steps.text: the agent has produced a draft recipe titled "Lemon Bars" with the category left blank
steps.observed: reused the draft from the pasted-text extraction above: title field "** Lemon Bars", Category "Unset"

steps.text: Maria sets the draft's category to "Dessert" and saves it
steps.command: agent-browser click @e6 (Dessert option) && agent-browser click @e8 (Save Recipe)

steps.text: "Lemon Bars" appears in Maria's recipe collection with category "Dessert"
steps.observed: row reads "** Lemon BarsDessert** lemonbaking" — category is correctly "Dessert", but the saved title is "** Lemon Bars", not the exact "Lemon Bars" the scenario names (same markdown-artifact defect as the extraction scenario above)

scenarios.rule: A Cook reviews and edits an agent-extracted draft before it is saved

steps.text: the agent has produced a draft recipe titled "Lemon Bars"
steps.command: agent-browser click @e3 (Extract Recipe, fresh /import page, pasted text only)
steps.observed: POST /api/recipe-import-agent/chat -> 200; draft shown titled "** Lemon Bars"; collection count was 4 before this action

steps.text: Maria discards the draft instead of saving it
"Lemon Bars" does not appear in Maria's recipe collection
steps.observed: 4 — unchanged from before the discarded draft was created, confirming no new row was added for it (the pre-existing "** Lemon Bars" row is the one already saved and asserted on in the preceding scenario, not this discarded one)
